question: Using the chain rule, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ if $$y=\sin\left((3x-1)^2\right).$$
explanation:
Identifying the composite functions
Let $$u=(3x-1)^2$$ so that $y=\sin u$.
Derivative of the outer function
$$\frac{dy}{du}=\cos u$$
Derivative of the inner function
$$\frac{du}{dx}=2(3x-1)\cdot 3=6(3x-1)$$
Applying the chain rule
$$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy}{du}\frac{du}{dx}=6(3x-1)\cos\left((3x-1)^2\right)$$
